newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods rise late amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods rise late amid tight supplies.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices edged higher late Wednesday, as perceived tightness in local supply offset a weak close in New York futures.
"Everybody's cutting runs," a broker said, observing that crude processing reductions at San Francisco refineries raised product prices to Los Angeles levels.
"There isn't any (gasoline) available," in the Bay, a broker said.
"Why would you run Alaska North Slope crude at $1.75 (below benchmark WTI) while (WTI) was at $25?" he said.
By contrast, NYMEX prices for January gasoline turned bearish after hitting technical resistance near 70 cents a gallon. The contract finished 0.89 cents lower at 68.24 cents.
NYMEX heating oil slipped 0.65 cents a gallon to 73.57 cents, following a weekly report Tuesday which showed a larger-than-expected distillate build of 1.8 million barrels.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles rose 0.50 cent a gallon to 74/75 cents, as ongoing production cutbacks trimmed output at Mobil and Texaco refineries in southern California.
Traders said scheduled January maintenance at refineries such as Tosco, Avon, Calif., and Mobil, Torrance, Calif., would kept supply concerns in traders thoughts near-term.
Bids for conventional gasoline in L.A. rose 0.50 cent to 65.50 cents a gallon, with Bay-area grades rising a notional 2.50 cents on the day to reach parity with L.A..
Bids for jet fuel rose 0.75 cents a gallon to 74.75 cents a gallon in L.A., on rumors of ongoing exports to Asia.
